name: Sikadur Hex-300
paste:
SIKADUR® HEX-300: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur® Hex-300, November 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/sikadur_hex-300.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur® Hex-300 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sikadur® Hex-300 is a two-component 100% solids, moisture-tolerant, high strength, high modulus epoxy. Sikadur® Hex-300 is an unfilled primer or impregnation resin with an extra-long pot life and a slow curing speed. Sikadur® Hex-300 is compliant with the 2012 and 2009 International
    - Building Codes (IBC) and the 1997 Uniform Building Code (UBC) per ICC-ES Evalutation Report ESR- 3288.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur® Hex-300 may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Impregnating resin for SikaWrap® fabric reinforcement for the wet application.
    - Primer resin for the wet application system.
    - Used as a seal coat and impregnating resin for horizontal and vertical applications.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur® Hex-300
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: HIGH-MODULUS, HIGH-STRENGTH, 2-PART EPOXY IMPREGNATING RESIN USED WITH SIKAWRAP STRUCTURAL STRENGTHENING SYSTEMS
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - 2009 & 2012 International Building Codes (IBC)
    - 1997 Uniform Building Code (UBC) per ICC-ES Evalutation Report ESR-3288.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ISO 527: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2).
    - EN 12614: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Glass transition temperature (p.2).
    - ASTM D 648: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Heat deflection temperature (p.2).
    - EN ISO 9514: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Pot Life (p.3).
    - AS5100.8:2017: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > SUBSTRATE QUALITY (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy mix and application by trowel and impregnation roller
    - Manufactured for manual or mechanical saturation methods
    - High mechanical properties
    - Extra-long pot life
    - Tolerant of moisture before, during and after cure
    - High strength, high modulus adhesive
    - Excellent adhesion to concrete, masonry metals, wood and most structural materials
    - Fully compatible and developed specifically for the SikaWrap® System
    - High temperature resistance
    - High abrasion and shock resistance
    - Solvent-free, VOC compliant
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Colour: Component A: light-yellow to amber liquid; Component B: pale yellow to clear liquid; Components A + B mixed: light-yellow to clear liquid
    - Density: 1.16 kg/l (component A+B mixed) (at +23 °C)
2.6 Viscosity.
    | Temperature | Viscosity |
    | +15 °C | ~2,000 cps |
    | +23 °C | ~700 cps |
    | +40 °C | ~200 cps |
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: 2,620 MPa (7 days) +23°C, 50%R.H
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~ 3,500 MPa (+23 °C, 50 % R.H); ~ 4,130 MPa (+60 °C, 50 % R.H, post cured min. 48hrs) (ASTM D-790)
    - Tensile strength: ~41 MPa (+23 °C, 50 % R.H); ~70 MPa (+23 °C, 50 % R.H, post cured min. 48hrs) (ASTM D-638)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~ 3,500 N/mm2 (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 3.2 % (+23 °C, 50 % R.H); 4.8 % (+60 °C, 50 % R.H, post cured min. 48hrs) (ASTM D-638)
    - Service temperature: -40 to +45 °C
2.8 Compressive strength.
    | 4 °C | 23 °C | 32 °C |
    | 3 days | - | ~55 MPa | - |
    | 7 days | ~7.0 MPa | ~75 MPa | >80 MPa |
    | 28 days | - | ~80 MPa | - |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (ASTM D-695)
    Note printed: Material cured and tested at the temperatures indicated and 50 % R.H.
2.9 Glass transition temperature.
    | Curing time | Curing temp | TG |
    | 30 days | +30 °C | +53 °C |
    Test method printed: (EN 12614)
2.10 Heat deflection temperature.
    | Curing time | Curing temp | HDT |
    | 7 days | +15 °C | +43 °C |
    | 7 days | +23 °C | +49 °C |
    | 3 days | +40 °C | +60 °C |
    | 7 days | +40 °C | +66 °C |
    Test method printed: (ASTM D 648)
2.11 System structure. Substrate primer - Sikadur®-330 / Sikadur® Hex-300. Impregnating/laminating resin - Sikadur® Hex-300. Structural strengthening fabric - SikaWrap® type to suit requirements.
2.12 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 15 lt kits
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production if stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging
    - Storage conditions: Store in original, unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - The substrate must be sound and of sufficient tensile strength to provide a minimum pull off strength of 1.5 N/mm2 or as per the requirements of the design specification ACI 440.2R, AS5100.8:2017 or Vic Roads Spec Section 688: 2018 .
    - See also the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual wet application" Ref 850 41 03 and the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® saturator machine wet application" Ref 850 41 04.
3.3 Substrate preparation. See the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual wet application" Ref 850 41 03 and the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® saturator machine wet application" Ref 850 41 04.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Mix entire unit, do not batch down
    - Consumption: See the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual wet application" Ref. 850 41 03 and the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® saturator machine wet application" Ref 850 41 04. Guide: 0.4–1.0 kg/m2.
    - Curing time: ~ 12–14 hours (Tack Free)
4.3 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Potlife | Open time |
    | +15 °C | ~6 hours | ~3 hours |
    | +23 °C | ~4 hours | – |
    | +40 °C | ~90 minutes | ~60 minutes |
    Test method printed: (EN ISO 9514)
    Note printed: The potlife begins when the resin and hardener are mixed. It is shorter at high temperatures and longer at low temperatures. The greater the quantity mixed, the shorter the potlife. To obtain longer workability at high temperatures, the mixed adhesive may be divided into portions. Another method is to chill components A+B before mixing them (not below +5 °C).
4.4 Mixing - Pre-batched units. Mix components A+B together for at least 3 minutes at low speed. Avoid aeration while mixing. Then, pour the whole mix into a clean container and stir again for approx. 1 more minute at low speed to keep air entrapment at a minimum.
4.5 Mixing - Bulk packing, not pre-batched. Add the components in the correct proportions into a suitable mixing pail and stir correctly using an electric low speed mixer as above for pre-batched units.
4.6 Application method / tools. See the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual wet application" Ref 850 41 03 and the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® saturator machine wet application" Ref 850 41 04.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all equipment immediately with Sika® Colma Cleaner. Cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - This product may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Sikadur® Hex-300 must be protected from rain for at least 24 hours after application. Ensure placement of fabric and laminating with roller takes place within open time.
    - For application in cold or hot conditions, pre-condition material for 24 hours in temperature controlled storage facilities to improve mixing, application and pot life limits.
    - For further information on over coating, number of layers or creep, please consult a structural engineer for calculations and see also the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual wet application" Ref 850 41 03 and the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® saturator machine wet application" Ref 850 41 04.
    - Sikadur® resins are formulated to have low creep under permanent loading. However due to the creep behaviour of all polymer materials under load, the long term structural design load must account for creep. Generally the long term structural design load must be lower than 20-25% of the failure load. Please consult a structural engineer for load calculations for your specific application.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +15 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.3 Dew point. Beware of condensation. Substrate temperature during application must be at least 3 °C above dew point.
5.4 Substrate moisture content. < 4 % pbw
5.5 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Sikadur® Hex-300 must be protected from rain for at least 24 hours after application. Ensure placement of fabric and laminating with roller takes place within open time.
    - For application in cold or hot conditions, pre-condition material for 24 hours in temperature controlled storage facilities to improve mixing, application and pot life limits.
5.6 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: 4 °C | 23 °C | 32 °C; 3 days | - | ~55 MPa | -; 7 days | ~7.0 MPa | ~75 MPa | >80 MPa; 28 days | - | ~80 MPa | - (ASTM D-695)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: 2,620 MPa (7 days) +23°C, 50%R.H
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~ 3,500 MPa (+23 °C, 50 % R.H); ~ 4,130 MPa (+60 °C, 50 % R.H, post cured min. 48hrs) (ASTM D-790)
    - Tensile strength: ~41 MPa (+23 °C, 50 % R.H); ~70 MPa (+23 °C, 50 % R.H, post cured min. 48hrs) (ASTM D-638)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~ 3,500 N/mm2 (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 3.2 % (+23 °C, 50 % R.H); 4.8 % (+60 °C, 50 % R.H, post cured min. 48hrs) (ASTM D-638)
    - Glass transition temperature: Curing time | Curing temp | TG; 30 days | +30 °C | +53 °C (EN 12614)
    - Heat deflection temperature: Curing time | Curing temp | HDT; 7 days | +15 °C | +43 °C; 7 days | +23 °C | +49 °C; 3 days | +40 °C | +60 °C; 7 days | +40 °C | +66 °C (ASTM D 648)
    - Pot Life: Temperature | Potlife | Open time; +15 °C | ~6 hours | ~3 hours; +23 °C | ~4 hours | –; +40 °C | ~90 minutes | ~60 minutes (EN ISO 9514)
    - Curing time: ~ 12–14 hours (Tack Free)
5.7 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.8 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur® Hex-300, November 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/sikadur_hex-300.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur® Hex 300 Part A, version 14/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/3/sds-sikadur-hex-300parta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
